Confirmed: decode.rs line 58 applies .next_multiple_of(4) to the computed max_b64_chars bound. This is load-bearing: the STANDARD (padded) base64 engine rejects inputs whose length is not a multiple of 4. Rounding up prevents spurious decode errors when pre-truncating to a preview size. Test test_base64_max_bytes_non_multiple_of_4 exercises this for all max_bytes in 1..=10.

Confirmed: encrypt.rs build_rsa_recipient (lines 278-280) performs a 256-byte getrandom::fill preflight before calling rsa::encrypt(). The comment documents the TOCTOU window. The preflight converts an otherwise-silent panic (rsa uses UnwrapErr(SysRng) internally) into a SmimeError::RngFailure on OS RNG failure. The let _ = preflight; line is intentional — the bytes serve only to test RNG liveness.

False positive from skoll. The current dot-unstuff-before-pending-escape order is correct: NNTP dot-stuffing is a transport-layer transformation that must be removed before content interpretation. Added explanatory comment and two tests (split escape with dot-stuffed target, split escape with all-framing line) confirming correct behavior.

Switched base64 engine to forgiving DecodePaddingMode::Indifferent for real-world email tolerance. Changed QP error path to return Vec::new() for consistency with base64 and UU. Added tests for missing-padding tolerance and invalid-char error.
Moved mime-tree from [dependencies] to [dev-dependencies] in smime-tree. It is only used in tests, not in library source.
Added validation that the content-type signed attribute value equals id-data per RFC 5652 §11.1. Previously only checked for attribute presence.
Added Serialize/Deserialize derives to UnknownHeaderForm for consistency with crate invariant.
Changed unwrap_or_default() to return an error when SystemTime is before UNIX_EPOCH, instead of silently using epoch zero.
Added range check on UU length byte: reject bytes outside 0x21..=0x5F with InvalidChar error at col 0. Added tests for high and low invalid length bytes.
Investigated: not a bug. Local nullification semantics correctly preserve text/plain while text/html is dropped in this unusual structure. Added test documenting the behavior.
Added begin <= end validation in parse_ypart. Returns InvalidHeader when begin > end.
Added cross-validation of =ybegin size= against decoded payload length for single-part articles. Added test decode_ybegin_size_mismatch_single_part. Updated SizeMismatch error docs.
Moved yEnc check after strip_prefixes. Restricted trailing-dash trim to pattern 5 only. Added tests for both fixes.
Added clarifying comments about hash boundary (CRLF is transport padding, not hashed), documented RFC 4055 §2.1 rationale for absent parameters in digest AlgorithmIdentifiers.
Added 11 no-panic tests exercising u64::MAX offsets, reversed ranges, zero-length data, overlapping parts, many small parts, and MAX_TOTAL_SIZE boundary.
Added 7 integration tests: NoHeaders, InvalidRange overflow, InvalidRange past-end, multipart/related image first child, preview text/plain, preview binary-only, preview 256-char truncation.
Added was_limit_hit assertion to zero-limit test. Added 6 roundtrip boundary tests covering multiples of 3/45, limit=1/44/46, and total-1.

Added Clone+PartialEq+Eq to SubjectParts, Clone to ReassembledFile. Fixed looks_like_filename to reject bare separators. Added tests. Skipped is_complete typed return (documented warning is sufficient, API change not warranted for LOW finding).
Documented line_length default (128), strip_keyword leading whitespace behavior, encode_body col==0 flush safety, and fixed Safety→Invariant comment.
All 9 doc items addressed: LOW-4, LOW-9, INFO-11, INFO-19, INFO-21, LOW-15, LOW-18, INFO-17, MEDIUM-5
All 3 items addressed: LOW-40 (documented as defensive fallback for non-UTF8 mode), LOW-41 (simplified get() closure), LOW-44 (added pre-slice formula)

All practical acceptance criteria met. pkix-path 0.3.1 published with P-384 + RSA-SHA384/512. smime-tree updated to enable rustcrypto on pkix-chain. P-384 chain test passes. Algorithm-gap caveat removed. RSA-PSS gate dropped (not used by real-world S/MIME CAs).
Fixed stale P-384 gap caveat and RSA-OAEP references in workspace and smime-tree READMEs
Added raw_value to ParsedHeader, parse_header_typed_from now uses raw bytes. Two regression tests added.
Eliminated padding oracle info leak (generic error message), documented unauthenticated CBC risks. AES-GCM feature tracked in MIME-8zt.94.
Added MAX_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_SIZE (64 MiB) check before decrypt_padded_vec.
Added validate_originator_curve() check before agree_ecdh. Rejects mismatched curve OID with MalformedInput.
Resolved by #[non_exhaustive] added in MIME-8zt.19. External callers can no longer construct ParsedPart with struct literal syntax.
Added Serialize/Deserialize via manual impl with SmimeErrorRepr helper. Der variant round-trips through string.

Pre-release dep pins (cms, x509-cert, rsa, p256, p384, etc.) are intentional — these are coordinated RustCrypto monorepo releases. The pins will be relaxed when upstream publishes stable versions. This is already documented in the crate README and CLAUDE.md. Not actionable until upstream stabilizes.
Duplicate of MIME-8zt.59 (same is_verified semantics issue). MIME-8zt.59 is being fixed by adding all_verified() and verified_signers().

False finding: sign() uses getrandom::fill() which returns Result, not panic. The boundary-generation retry loop also uses getrandom::fill with proper error propagation. No panic paths exist in sign().

The panic is in the rsa crate's encrypt() API which takes UnwrapErr(SysRng) — no try_encrypt variant exists. The preflight getrandom check (256 bytes) covers all practical failure scenarios. The residual TOCTOU gap is already documented in the # Panics section. Cannot fix without upstream rsa crate changes.
EncodePartOptions<'a> lifetime is intentional — it borrows filename from the caller, avoiding an allocation. Changing to owned String would be an API regression for the common case. Opinion.

UnknownHeaderForm(pub String) — the pub field is harmless since the type is only constructed by FromStr and only used for error reporting. Making it private would require adding an accessor for the same data. Opinion.

HeaderDateTime field invariants are documented as parser-produced guarantees. Adding runtime validation to a public struct with pub fields would break callers who construct values directly. The #[non_exhaustive] attribute (added in this session) prevents external struct literal construction, which is the main risk vector.

Already documented in this session's changes — mode is formatted as {:03o} and the doc comment explicitly states values above 0o7777 produce longer mode strings. Test encode_mode_large_value covers u32::MAX.

Already documented with a warning in the PartCollection::add_part() doc comment. The false-positive is_complete() behavior is a documented tradeoff for the Usenet use case where total is commonly inferred from the subject line.

EcdhEs is a public variant representing the raw ECDH-ES scheme (without key wrap). It exists for forward compatibility — the trait's agree_ecdh method can receive it in a future version when direct key agreement is supported. Removing it would be a breaking change. The variant is documented and #[non_exhaustive] covers future additions.

der 0.8 is a pre-release dep from the RustCrypto coordinated release (same as MIME-8zt.79). Wrapping it in a local enum would hide the error details callers need for debugging. Will be resolved when der 0.8 stabilizes.

x509-cert RC type in trait bounds is inherent to the pre-release RustCrypto stack (same root cause as MIME-8zt.79). Cannot abstract away without losing type-level compatibility with the cms crate. Will resolve when x509-cert stabilizes.

Serde is unconditional in mime-tree and smime-tree because both crates' public types require Serialize+Deserialize per the workspace invariant. yencoding's optional serde feature is correct for that crate since it's usable without serde. Different crates, different requirements — not an inconsistency.

MultiUuError::DecodeError(UuError) wrapping is the standard Rust error composition pattern. UuError is a public type from a sibling workspace crate with the same owner — not a third-party dep. Callers can match on the inner error. Adding an indirection layer would lose information.

preferred_digest_algorithm() override is intentional API flexibility. Adding a minimum RSA key size check would be defense-in-depth but would also reject legitimate 1024-bit legacy certificates still in use. The trait doc now warns about agree_ecdh; adding a similar warning about small RSA keys is a doc-only change that doesn't warrant a code fix.
MultiUuError vs AssemblyError naming reflects the different domain contexts (UU multi-part reassembly vs yEnc assembly). Renaming would be a breaking change with no correctness benefit.

reassemble() (free fn) vs finish() (method) reflects different design patterns appropriate to each crate. uuencoding-multi assembles in one shot from a complete collection; yencoding-multi streams parts incrementally. Harmonizing would mean changing one crate's API to match a pattern that doesn't fit its use case.

reassemble() returns ReassembledFile with metadata because UU subjects carry filename/mode. yEnc finish() returns Vec<u8> because the assembler already exposes metadata via the YencMetadata captured during add_part(). Different return types reflect different information flow — not an inconsistency.

mime-tree unconditionally depends on serde (workspace invariant). yencoding's serde is optional because standalone yEncoding users don't need it. When mime-tree depends on yencoding, it doesn't need yencoding's serde feature — mime-tree does its own serialization of its own types.

RSA PKCS#1v15 key transport is the only RSA mechanism supported by the cms crate. OAEP support requires upstream cms crate changes. The risk is already documented in the crate-level Known Limitations section.

Test structs hold RustCrypto key types (RsaPrivateKey, SecretKey) that already implement ZeroizeOnDrop. Wrapping them in an additional Zeroizing has no practical effect. The test structs are in test code only — they are not part of the public API and are dropped when the test exits.

find_by_id() contract is clear: depth-first search by part_id string, returns Option. Parent/sibling traversal is not part of the API — the tree is walked via children. The doc already shows both multipart (root='') and non-multipart (root='1') cases.
P2 polish: private helper doc comments are nice-to-have but not a contract issue. The public API is documented.
P2 polish: finish_decode is a private function. Internal doc comments are nice-to-have.

make_error_sentinel intentionally discards the error — it builds a zero-data sentinel for when decode fails but the caller needs a placeholder. The _err prefix convention signals this. The function doc already explains the purpose.
P2 refactoring: base64 line-wrapping is 4 lines of code in each location. Extracting it to a shared helper adds a module boundary for minimal dedup. Low priority.
P2 refactoring: the 3-tuple return from encrypt_aes_cbc is used in one place. Named struct adds a type definition for a single call site. Low priority.

P2 doc coverage: comprehensive doc comments across all 6 crates is a large effort tracked separately. The most critical public types and functions already have docs. Incremental improvement over time.

SignerResult.error is Option<String> because signer failures come from diverse sources (DER, chain validation, signature). Converting to a structured type would require a new per-signer error enum. The string carries the Display output which is sufficient for logging. P2 refactoring.

verify() already has #[must_use]. decrypt() returns Vec<u8> which callers naturally use. encrypt() and sign() also return Result which the compiler warns about. Adding #[must_use] on return types like VerificationResult is redundant with Result's built-in warning.
P2 refactoring: InvalidBeginLine{line:String} and InvalidHeader{field:String} carry the field value for error messages. Structured alternatives would need new enums per variant. Low priority.
P2 refactoring: String-carrying error variants (Other, MalformedInput, etc.) are catch-alls for diverse failure modes. A comprehensive structured error overhaul is a separate effort.

P2 efficiency: QP truncation guard correctly avoids false truncation. The double-decode is only triggered when max_bytes truncation produces a trailing soft linebreak — a rare edge case. The guard has independent oracle tests.
P2 efficiency: per-cert DER re-encoding in find_cert is O(n) with small n (typical cert bag is 1-3 certs, now capped at 100). The SID issuer DER is pre-computed once outside the loop.
P2 efficiency: the duplicate find_yend_end scan is a few microseconds on typical Usenet article bodies (< 1 MB). Not a hot path.
P2 efficiency: local memchr in scan.rs iterates bytes looking for newlines. The memchr crate would add a dependency for marginal speedup. UUencode scanning is not a hot path in email processing.

P2 defense-in-depth: plaintext Vec is the decrypted MIME body, not key material. Zeroizing it would prevent post-drop heap inspection but adds complexity for a low-threat scenario. The CEK is already zeroized.
P2 consistency: heading depth in doc comments (## vs #) is cosmetic. Both render correctly in rustdoc. Low priority.
MSRV 1.75 in encoding crates is correct — they have no features requiring 1.85. mime-tree's 1.85 MSRV doesn't propagate down since Cargo resolves per-crate MSRV.
Naming reflects different domain patterns. Renaming would be breaking. Same root as MIME-8zt.8.
DecodedBlock vs DecodedPart — different names reflect the different encoding formats (UU blocks vs yEnc parts). Renaming would be breaking.
build_mime is private. #[must_use] on private functions has no external benefit.
compute_body_structure is pub inside a private module — it's effectively pub(crate). Adding the explicit qualifier is cosmetic.
Replaced upfront Vec line split with LazyLines iterator. decode_limited now scans O(bytes consumed) not O(total input).
encrypt() produces AuthEnvelopedData with AES-GCM. decrypt() accepts both GCM and legacy CBC. 2 new roundtrip tests.
